title: A w-contractible affine pro-etale object is weakly contractible
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in the universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be an object of this site. Suppose that every faithfully flat ring map $A\to B$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] which is weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] admits a ring retraction $B\to A$, whose composite with $A\to B$ is $\mathrm{id}_A$. Then for every epimorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets on the full site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, the evaluation map $F(T)\to G(T)$ is surjective. Here a sheaf of sets is a contravariant set-valued functor on the site satisfying unique gluing of compatible sections on every covering; a morphism is a natural transformation, and an epimorphism is a morphism that is right-cancellable among such morphisms.

proof.text: Let $\varphi:F\to G$ be an epimorphism of sheaves of sets and $s\in G(T)$. The epimorphism/local-surjectivity equivalence gives a covering $\{f_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ in $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and sections $t_i\in F(T_i)$ with $\varphi(t_i)=s|_{T_i}$.

The underlying family is a pro-etale covering of the affine scheme $T$. Apply the covering-section lemma using exactly the ring splitting hypothesis of the item. It gives $\sigma:T\to C=\coprod_iT_i$ with $p\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_T$, where $p|_{T_i}=f_i$. This is an assertion about schemes; no change from the small site to a big site is needed.

The coprojections have disjoint clopen images covering $C$. Their inverse images $U_i=\sigma^{-1}(T_i)$ are disjoint clopen opens covering $T$, and $\sigma|_{U_i}$ factors through $T_i$, with composite to $T$ the inclusion $U_i\hookrightarrow T$. Quasi-compactness of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ gives finitely many of the $U_i$ covering $T$; disjointness forces all the remaining $U_i$ to be empty. An open immersion is flat because its maps on local rings are isomorphisms, and its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence flat; thus each $U_i\to T$ is weakly etale. Composition stability makes $U_i\to X$ an object of the small site, within the original size bound. These finitely many opens form a pro-etale covering: for any affine test open $V\subset T$, take affine neighborhoods in the intersections $V\cap U_i$ and then a finite subcover of $V$. Thus their images have union exactly $V$.

proof.text: Restrict $t_i$ along $\sigma|_{U_i}:U_i\to T_i$, obtaining $u_i\in F(U_i)$. Naturality gives $\varphi(u_i)=s|_{U_i}$ since $f_i\circ\sigma|_{U_i}$ is the inclusion. The empty scheme is a site object with an empty covering, so both sheaves have exactly one section there. Hence the $u_i$ agree on every pairwise intersection, which is empty for distinct indices. The sheaf axiom glues them to $u\in F(T)$; the restrictions of $\varphi(u)$ and $s$ agree on the covering, so sheaf uniqueness gives $\varphi(u)=s$. The same argument applies to an empty covering when $A$ is the zero ring.
